To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we have developed a novel platform for the study of tissue macrophages using iPSCs.
we show that human and mouse iPSC can recapitulate yolk sac (embryonic) hematopoiesis.
iPSCs derived primitive macrophage like iMacs provide a platform for modeling the differentiation and function of tissue resident macro phages.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the generation of macrophages from human pluripotent stem cell (hPSC).
the development of a novel cell therapy for the treatment of ischemic stroke, using a novel cell type, the induced pluripotent macrophage.
understanding how tissue resident macrophagess are generated in vivo and how to generate these cells in vitro for use in modeling disease, screening for therapeutics, and cell based therapies.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
iMacs constitute an important platform for studying tissue resident macrophases.
iPSC-derived macrophage like iMacs can differentiate into functional tissue-resident macrophage-like cells with the help of organ specific cues.
iPSC-derived macrophages can be differentiated into tissue specific macrophages with organ specific cues.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we developed a method to generate primitive macrophages from iPSCs and demonstrated that these cells can differentiate into functional tissue macrophages with organ specific cues.

we developed a method for the derivation of tissue resident macro phages in vitro from human and mouse iPSC, and we demonstrated that these cells can be used to study tissue resident macroph age differentiation and function, as well as disease modeling and drug discovery.

The main takeaway from our work is that
iMacs constitute an excellent platform for studying tissue macrophages, as well as for modeling tissue macrophage differentiation and function.

iPSC derived primitive hematopoietic cells (iHem) can be differentiated into primitive macrophages in vitro and further differentiated into tissue specific macrophage like cell populations in vitro or in vivo.
iPSC derived macrophage like (iMacs), which are generated from iPSCs, can differentiate into functional tissue macrophage-like cells in vitro and in vivo.
